limitations.title: Shared seats
limitations.desc: Seats are pooled to keep pricing low. Your work stays isolated; group-wide fair-use caps keep everyone online.

limitations.title: Daily quotas
limitations.desc: Heavy exports and audits are limited per day so one member can’t burn the whole group’s credits. Resets every 24h.

limitations.title: No Semrush API
limitations.desc: Access is through dashboard + extension. Official Semrush API endpoints are not part of standard group buy plans.

limitations.title: Fair use
limitations.desc: No bots or aggressive scraping. That keeps shared accounts stable for the whole pool.

article.ctaQuestion: Ready to compare plans and pick a tier?
article.overviewText: Below is a simple guide. You will see what you get. You will see the main ideas for this topic. You will also get a short checklist before you choose a plan.
benefitsList: Dashboard access to real Semrush modules (not a fake “viewer”).
Tools you already use like Keyword Magic Site Audit Position Tracking and Domain Overview on supported tiers.
Fast onboarding. Pay log in and start work without a long sales process.
Shared infrastructure with fair-use rules so the pool stays stable for everyone.
article.mainPointsSuffix: simple. Know what is included. Know what is limited. Pick a plan tier that fits how you work day to day.
preSubscribeList: Confirm the modules you need are in the plan you are comparing.
Expect daily or fair-use caps on heavy exports and large audits.
Use one primary session where possible; simultaneous sessions can hit limits faster.
Read the transparency section on your provider for refunds and support hours.
article.summaryText: If you want the short version focus on stability and limits. Also check that your plan includes the modules you use most.
summaryList: Group buy access runs through a secure dashboard; feature set follows your tier.
Limits exist to protect uptime. Plan your heaviest reports accordingly.
Pricing scales from Lite-style extension use up to agency-oriented bundles.
When in doubt, start on a mid tier and upgrade if you outgrow credits or tools.
